title: Successive Percentage Change: Don't Just Add
excerpt: A 20% increase followed by a 10% decrease is NOT a net 10% increase. Percentages compound — apply each change to the current value, not the original.
author: BountyCode Team
body:
## The trap

"Price increased 20%, then decreased 10%. What is the net change?"

Most students answer 10% (20 − 10). That is wrong.

## Why

The 10% decrease applies to the *new* (higher) price, not the original.

100 × 1.20 = 120, then 120 × 0.90 = 108. Net change = +8%, not +10%.

## Rule

Apply each change one after another:
Final = Original × (1 ± x/100) × (1 ± y/100)

## Practice it

Take the Percentages timed topic test — it includes successive-change questions.
code:
original = 100
after_increase = original * 1.20   # 120
after_decrease = after_increase * 0.90  # 108
net = (after_decrease - original) / original * 100  # 8.0%
